There is no reality in which masks do not work, in which Trump has done more than any president but Lincoln for black Americans that supports Trump's ridiculous claims of Obama's interference in his election campaign or any of his ludicrous lies. There is reality, and there is the disgusting, anti-science, anti-woman, racist fantasy for white men that Trump is creating in a pathetic attempt to keep and hold his power. Reality is that Donald Trump should not have the ability to direct military action without congressional approval. No president should, but especially not this president, who is a slave to his own worst impulses and has no tether to the real world in which we all exist. Congress needs to revoke the standing use of force authorization to this president and to any future president. The act of war is too dangerous, too deadly, and too important to leave in the hands of any single individual, including individual women. Sorry, not sorry is executive produced by Alyssa Milano. That's me. Our associate producer is Ben Jackson, editing and engineering by Natasha Jacobs and music by Josh Cook, Alicia Eagle, and Milo Bouliari. That's my boy. Please subscribe on Spotify, iTunes, or wherever you get your podcasts. And if you like the show, please rate, review, and spread the word. Sorry, not sorry.

explicit_propositions.text: Donald Trump presents a false dichotomy between evidence-based and faith-based realities.
There is only one objective reality.
Masks are effective at preventing disease transmission.
No president should have unilateral authority to initiate military action.
Trump has not done more than Lincoln for Black Americans.
Trump’s claims about Obama interfering in his election are baseless.
Trump repeatedly makes false statements.
Trump promotes a racist, anti-science, and anti-woman ideology.
Trump lacks grounding in objective reality.
Congress should revoke the standing authorization for use of military force against Trump and future presidents.

assumptions.text: Objective truth exists independently of personal belief or political narrative.
Scientific consensus constitutes reliable evidence about public health measures like mask usage.
Historical achievements of U.S. presidents can be objectively evaluated using measurable criteria.
Political leaders should be held accountable based on verifiable facts rather than emotional appeal.
The separation of powers, particularly congressional oversight over war, is essential to democratic integrity.
Executive power over military decisions poses a serious threat when unchecked.
The audience values scientific reasoning, historical accuracy, and democratic norms.
Public discourse benefits from challenging narratives that promote falsehoods.
Podcast audiences are capable of distinguishing credible analysis from partisan rhetoric.
Media creators have moral responsibility to challenge harmful ideologies through their platforms.
